title: Feedback and expectation alignment
task_statement: Set measurable expectations, review triggers, and consequences for a production model. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Workspace spend and rate limits
components.first_principle: Spend limits cap monthly spend for one workspace, and rate limits cap requests and tokens per minute.
steps: Create one workspace for each team or environment.
Scope each API key to the workspace it serves.
Set rate limits for each model in the workspace.
Set a monthly spend limit for the workspace.
Configure alerts at the spend thresholds.
Check the limits again after a model or traffic change. (Inference)
pros: Caps spend and requests for each workspace on its own.
Sends alerts before the spend cap applies.
Keeps each team cost visible in its own workspace.
cons: Spend limits cannot be set on the Default Workspace.
Requests above a rate limit fail with a 429 error.
use_when: A team or project needs its own budget.
An environment needs lower limits than production.
do_not_use_when: One small project has no budget owner. (Inference)
The traffic has no budget or capacity requirement. (Inference)

components.name: Feedback contract with review triggers
components.first_principle: A written trigger turns a metric drift into a scheduled review. (Inference)
steps: Set the primary metric and its threshold with the owner. (Inference)
Derive the error budget from the threshold for each period. (Inference)
Write each review trigger as a count or a rate, not a judgment. (Inference)
Name the consequence of each trigger before launch. (Inference)
Write the rule that separates tuning from a rebuild. (Inference)
Review the contract on the same date as the requirements. (Inference)
pros: Turns metric drift into a scheduled review. (Inference)
Settles the breach question before a dispute starts. (Inference)
cons: A trigger can fire on a data change instead of a model change. (Inference)
A strict consequence can pause work after a false alarm. (Inference)
use_when: Production traffic depends on a probabilistic output. (Inference)
A stakeholder asks for a guaranteed percentage. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: A prototype has no users and no budget. (Inference)
The metric has no measurement yet. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Name the owner who signs each consequence. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Date the contract and review it with the requirements. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Route each trigger to a named owner. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Segment the data before any rebuild decision. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Forecast monthly spend from cost per task and expected volume. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Add a cost trigger for drift above the forecast. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set a latency range instead of a single point. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D6.3. Expect a drift or SLA dispute. The credited answer applies the agreed trigger and rule, not a new target. (Inference)
components.trap: A higher SLA target looks like a fix, but the system behavior does not change. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Write each trigger, its owner, and its consequence before launch. (Inference)
components.exam_tip: A drop below the agreed iterate threshold calls for tuning, not a rebuild. (Inference)

flowchart LR
  M[Metric threshold] --> B[Error budget]
  B --> T[Review trigger]
  T --> O[Named owner]
  O --> R{Iterate or rebuild}
  R --> I[Tune and re-measure]
  R --> X[Re-architect]

patterns.wording: a quality drop below an agreed range
patterns.rule: Run the agreed review and tune before any rebuild.
traps: Tighten the target to hide the drop

patterns.wording: a stakeholder demands a perfect guarantee
patterns.answer_type: measured range with a named trigger
patterns.rule: Replace the guarantee with a measured range, a trigger, and a consequence.
traps: Promise a single point with no range
